criteria.source: fairness audit: does the baseline work in its own regime on our faults
criteria.description: Under bounded noise, a one-MVM line-level Wei & Roth arm (worst-case or random-noise threshold) reaches line F1 >= 0.9 on >= 3 of 4 k at each of sigma 1% and 2%. PASS means the baseline is not a strawman: any "fails at 1-2% noise" sentence about Wei & Roth must then be dropped. FAIL means the paper's guarantee (outliers > 2 rho delta ||x||) does not cover our moderate-magnitude stuck faults, and the paper states that regime mismatch instead of "Wei & Roth fails".

criteria.source: H8-CS-2x rule under the Wei & Roth noise model
criteria.description: Under bounded noise, forward-only CS needs >= 2x fewer reads than the best W-R cell-level arm (or W-R misses F1 0.9 while CS reaches it) on >= 3 of 4 k at each of sigma 1% and 2%.

criteria.source: H8-CSF-2x rule re-measured with the frozen E5 arms under H8's Gaussian noise
criteria.description: Same as E5-CS-2x-bounded under Gaussian read noise (H8's setting, E5 arms).

criteria.source: H8-kill applied to the Wei & Roth noise model
criteria.description: Kill the "fewer reads than Wei & Roth" wording if, under bounded noise, a W-R cell arm reaches F1 0.9 with no more reads than forward-only CS on >= 2 of 4 k at sigma 1% or at sigma 2%.
Forward-only CS cell F1 below 0.8 on any 1-2% row under either noise model.

Cost on the paper's axis (r_cols, col_equiv), line-level F1 of all arms including the *_R variants, sigma 4% rows, the guarantee flag (paper_guarantee_form), H8 ROTH reads/F1 joined as h8_*, per-instance table (eval_instances.csv). The line-level arms and the cell-level extension are reported in separate columns and must stay separate in the paper.
